summary: Shows using `meta: flush_handlers` in a rescue section so notified handlers still run after an error. Describes the `ansible_failed_task` and `ansible_failed_result` variables available in rescue (since 2.1) and using them in conditions.
questions: How do I make sure handlers still run if a task fails?
How can I tell which task failed inside my rescue section?
How do I get the result of the failed task in rescue?

answer_card.title: Handlers and failure info in rescue
answer_card.answer_md:
Run notified handlers even after an error by flushing them in `rescue`:
```yaml
    rescue:
      - name: Make sure all handlers run
        meta: flush_handlers
```

In `rescue` you get two variables (added in 2.1):
- `ansible_failed_task`: the task that failed, e.g. `ansible_failed_task.name`.
- `ansible_failed_result`: its captured return value, like using `register`.

```yaml
    rescue:
      - when: ansible_failed_task.name == 'Do Something'
        ansible.builtin.debug:
          msg: All is good, ignore error
      - when: "'/bin/false' in ansible_failed_result.cmd | d([])"
        ansible.builtin.fail:
          msg: It is still false!!!
```
